chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I stand and pray in Mecca, and a woman is seated in front of me, or passes by.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem. Rather, it was named Bakkah because therein men and women wail (or weep/cry out).'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in Mecca with a woman sitting in front of you?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the presence of a woman in front of the pray-er does not invalidate the prayer in Mecca, distinguishing it from other locations where a *satar* (screen) is required. He provides the etymological reasoning for the name 'Bakkah,' linking it to the intense supplication and wailing of worshippers, thereby highlighting the spiritual atmosphere of the Sacred Mosque. This ruling underscores the unique status of the Kaaba as the primary focal point (*qibla*) where the barrier between the worshipper and the Divine House is minimized.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I stand and Pray Salaat in Makkah, and the woman is seated in front of him, or passes by’. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem. But rather, Makkah has been named as Bakkah, because therein ‘تَبُكُّ’ wail (Baka’a) the men and the women’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
I stand up for Salat (prayer) in Makkah and a woman is sitting in front of me or is passing. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful. It is called Bakkah because both men and women weep there.’”
